evidence.note: PKCE plain is used; this is what the security review flagged
With plain, the challenge equals the verifier, so anyone who sees the authorization request can redeem the code
Code was returned with state, and there is no error

output.fix: Switch the mobile app to PKCE S256. Generate a high-entropy random code_verifier (43–128 characters). Send code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) with code_challenge_method=S256. Configure the authorization server to reject plain for public clients. Keep the exact-match redirect URI registration and keep verifying state on return. Prefer claimed HTTPS or app-link redirects over custom schemes.

alternatives.why_not: Under plain, the verifier equals the challenge, so they match. The problem is the weak method, not a mismatch.
